dossier.public_summary: The 1.83-day dip is very deep and V-shaped and odd and even dips differ by ~13% with high significance, implying a binary at twice the period. Individual transits and sectors show large depth changes. The implied size (~22 Earth radii) and Gaia RUWE 12.98 binary sign confirm this is not a planet transit on the target.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by 14.5k ppm (12.6%) at 51 sigma, opposite a secondary null. Consistent odd/even difference is required for a planet; a 2:1 alias binary naturally gives different eclipse depths with no secondary at half-phase.
Extremely V-shaped light curve with ingress ~45% of duration and high impact parameter favours a grazing eclipse, not a flat-bottomed planet transit.

Depth is not constant between sectors (p <<0.01) and transit_depths p_consistent 0.0 chi2 3334.26034582299 with outliers at -18.8 sigma shows depth changes transit-to-transit. For an on-target signal this variability, combined with V shape and odd/even difference, points to a stellar eclipse rather than aperture/alignment.

Implied companion size at 0.33 stellar radii (~22 Earth radii) is above the planet limit and corresponds to a large Jupiter-sized star/EB, consistent with the V shape and odd/even difference, even though centroid verdict on_target offset_arcsec 0.2217 offset_sigma 0.2192 rules out neighbouring NEB.
Independent scorer ranks as highly unlike a planet, supporting the binary interpretation over the planet case.
